title: Raichandani's 93 Powers India U19 Past Afghanistan Into Asia Cup Final
excerpt: India chased 228 with 79 balls to spare at Al Amerat, winning by eight wickets after Ishan Sood's 3-43 sparked an Afghan collapse — Pakistan await in Saturday's final.
body:
• India Under-19 beat Afghanistan Under-19 by eight wickets in the second semi-final of the ACC Men's U19 Asia Cup at Al Amerat, Oman, on Thursday, November 12.
  • Afghanistan made 227 for 8 in 50 overs (Noman Sarafzai 51, Shah Faisal Rahimi 51; Ishan Sood 3-43) after a middle-order collapse undid a platform of 143 for 3.
  • Captain Lakshya Raichandani's 93 off 90 balls, with half-centuries from Aaryavir Sehwag (51) and VK Vineeth (57 not out), took India to 230 for 2 in 36.5 overs, with 79 balls to spare.
  • India meet Pakistan in the final on Saturday, November 14 — a rematch of last year's title clash, which Pakistan won.

India Under-19 are through to another Asia Cup final. Chasing 228 against Afghanistan in the second semi-final at Al Amerat on Thursday, India reached 230 for 2 in just 36.5 overs to win by eight wickets, captain Lakshya Raichandani's 93 off 90 balls setting up a title clash with Pakistan on Saturday.

Afghanistan's innings falls away

"Afghanistan's innings falls away Afghanistan won the toss and chose to bat, and for two-thirds of the innings the decision looked sound."

Afghanistan won the toss and chose to bat, and for two-thirds of the innings the decision looked sound. Noman Sarafzai and Shah Faisal Rahimi both made 51, and at 143 for 3 in the 36th over Afghanistan had wickets in hand and a platform to attack the closing overs. Instead the innings lost its way: three wickets fell in quick succession, with Aryan Savsani striking twice in a single over to dismiss Amir Hamza and Tahir Sarwary.

Ishan Sood was the pick of India's bowlers with 3 for 43, Savsani took 2 for 29, and captain Sohail Khan's unbeaten 36 off 44 balls carried Afghanistan to 227 for 8 — a total that, on a pitch offering little to the bowlers, always looked a touch short.

Raichandani takes the chase away

India's reply removed any tension early. Raichandani attacked through the off side, hitting 13 fours and a six, and put on 117 for the first wicket with Aaryavir Sehwag, whose 51 came off 57 balls. After Sehwag fell shortly after his half-century, Raichandani added 77 for the second wicket with VK Vineeth to shut Afghanistan out of the game.

Raichandani fell seven runs short of a century, but Vineeth finished the job, ending unbeaten on 57 off 62 balls and sealing the win with a six off Noor Ali Niazi. Yashbardhan Chauhan was unbeaten on 16 off 14 at the other end. Raichandani was named Player of the Match. The full scorecard is on Cricbuzz, and our earlier semi-final preview traced how both sides reached this stage.

An India-Pakistan final, again

Pakistan reached the final earlier in the day, beating Bangladesh by nine wickets in the first semi-final, Rizwanullah taking 5 for 30. Saturday's final at the same Al Amerat ground gives India the chance to avenge two defeats: Pakistan beat them in last year's final, and won again when the sides met in this edition's group stage, by three wickets on the back of an unbeaten century from Hamza Zahoor.

For India, the semi-final offered a cleaner template than the group-stage meeting: early wickets with the new ball, a squeeze through the middle overs, and a top three in form. Whether that holds against Pakistan's attack is the question Saturday will answer.
